problem:
Compute the sum of the first $6$ terms of the geometric series $-4+1-\frac{1}{4}+⋯.$

Express your answer as a fraction (do not round your answer).

${S}_{6}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio.

In our case, ${a}_{1}=-4.$ To find the value of $r,$ we find the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{1}{-4}=-\frac{1}{4}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=-4,\,N=6,$ and $r=-\frac{1}{4}$ into our formula, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{6} & =-4\cdot \frac{(1-{(-\frac{1}{4})}^{6})}{(1-(-\frac{1}{4}))} \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{6})}{(1+\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{(\frac{{4}^{6}-1}{{4}^{6}})}{(\frac{5}{4})} \\  & =-\frac{16}{5}\cdot (\frac{{4}^{6}-1}{{4}^{6}}) \\  & =-\frac{16}{5}\cdot \frac{4\,095}{4\,096} \\  & =-\frac{819}{256}\end{aligned}
$$
